text:
rachel: Quick sync — found a weird split-brain in staging during a cross-mode failover (dedicated -> hosted -> private). Two things: proxy token metadata leaking tenant-identifiers to hosted logs, and cache-epoch mismatch causing stale reads.

ben: Saw that. Hosted fallback issued a proxy token with an `orig_tenant` field in plaintext. If an operator runs ad-hoc log collection, they can see tenant ids. We should encrypt or HMAC that field.

yuki: Agreed. Also the cache-epoch header from the client was `42` but the private side had already rolled to `44` due to an operator-initiated rebind, so reads succeeded against old namespace and then were rejected on write. That's the race.

tom: Proposal summary: 1) proxy_token must carry only an opaque claim (proxy_label) + mac, not raw tenant ids; 2) runtime must expose X-Cache-Epoch and require clients to include it on every read/write; server rejects if header < current_epoch; 3) introduce TRANSIT proxy_mode for operator-approved transient forwarding with very short TTLs.

rachel: Sketch of proxy token shape:
```yaml
proxy_token:
  proxy_label: "p-abc123"   # opaque
  mac: "hmac-base64(...)"
  scopes: ["inference:read"]
  ttl: 30s
```
No orig_tenant in plaintext. Telemetry sidecar can unwrap mapping p-abc123 -> tenant after authenticating to KMS.

ben: For cache-epoch behavior, recommend: server maintains epoch N, when binding changes it increments to N+1 and sets transition_policy=quarantine by default. Quarantine semantics: reads with epoch < N+1 are allowed for a grace window (rebind_grace_seconds) but writes are rejected with HTTP 409 and error code `stale_cache_epoch`. Clients should handle 409 by re-handshaking.

yuki: That helps. Also add an auditing rule: any operator-initiated proxy_mode=transit must be recorded with operator_id + approval_id and be visible in audit trail. We can't silently flip proxy modes.

tom: Short manifest example for TRANSIT mode:
```yaml
handshake:
  src: dedicated
  dst: private
  proxy_mode: transit
  proxy_ttl: 30s
  rebind_grace_seconds: 20
  cache_transition: quarantine
  audit_level: high
```

rachel: Edgecase: what if transit proxy issued and private returns `require_rebind` while hosted is still proxying? We should force proxy invalidation on require_rebind with a small propagation window. Runtime state machine: PROXY_ISSUED -> PROXY_ACTIVE -> PROXY_REVOKE_NOTICE -> QUIESCE -> REBIND. Emit events: handshake.proxy.issued, handshake.proxy.revoked(reason), cache.epoch_roll.

ben: Also add a deterministic backoff for clients in case of repeated 409s: exponential backoff with jitter + a hard cap at rebind_grace_seconds to avoid thundering herd on rebind.

yuki: I'll draft the RFC delta: add proxy_mode=transit, make proxy_token opaque label-only, add `stale_cache_epoch` 409 semantics, and default cache_transition=quarantine. We'll include sample SDK helper pseudocode for handling 409 and automatic rehandshake.

infra-bot: infra-bot: canary "transit-probe" scheduled on runtime-canary at 07:20 UTC :white_check_mark:

tom: Action items: yuki drafts RFC patch + SDK pseudocode, ben implements proxy_token mac validation and telemetry unwrap hook, rachel writes audit checklist for operator approvals. Keep defaults conservative.

rachel: Thanks — let's not ship any plaintext tenant markers in proxy tokens. :no_entry_sign:
